name: Mebolazine (Dymethazine)

card.summary: A withdrawn oral steroid, a dimer of methasterone, that resurfaced in gray-market supplements; no human studies exist.
card.note: FDA has taken legal action against supplements containing it.

quick.overview:
Mebolazine is an oral anabolic steroid that was once sold as a medicine and later withdrawn. It reappeared from about 2008 in gray-market supplements.

No clinical studies were found.
quick.mechanism: It is reportedly a prodrug of methasterone, an androgen receptor agonist.
quick.risks: The FDA has acted against makers of supplements containing it, and it is classed with hepatotoxic oral steroids. Human safety data are absent.

lead: Mebolazine, also called dimethazine or dymethazine, is a synthetic, orally active anabolic-androgenic steroid. It is a 17α-alkylated derivative of dihydrotestosterone and an unusual dimer of methasterone, two units joined by an azine group [1]. People who seek it are after the usual outcome of anabolic steroids: more lean muscle mass and a larger, harder-looking physique.

Wikipedia reports that it reportedly acts as a prodrug of methasterone and that it was once marketed as the medicines Dostalon and Roxilon but is no longer sold [1]. Since about 2008 it has been found as an unlisted ingredient in some dietary supplements, and the US FDA has taken legal action against manufacturers of such products [1]. Case reports describe it as one of the designer steroids found in a product sold as a supplement, Super DMZ Rx 2.0 [2].
No clinical trials of its effects on muscle were found. The literature consists of metabolism studies and case reports of adverse events linked to supplements that contained it [1][2][3].

chain: Oral steroid is taken (reportedly as a prodrug of methasterone)
Muscle growth and lean mass are expected to increase
angle.text: The compound is sought for the muscle-building effects of androgens. It reappeared in gray-market supplements marketed for muscle gain, and no clinical trial has measured its effect on physique.

infobox: Withdrawn drug; found as undeclared supplement ingredient [1][3]

paras: It is classified as an androgen receptor agonist and is reported to act as a prodrug of methasterone [1]. A 2016 study examined its metabolism in vitro and in vivo [1].

Wikipedia notes use since 2008 as an illegal ingredient in dietary supplements, including some sold as vitamin B products, with FDA legal action against makers [1]. A 2015 review in Andrology discussed the growing presence of designer androgens in over-the-counter supplements [1].

A 2023 Steroids paper analysed about 16 New York residents who reported fatigue, hair loss and muscle aches between 2012 and 2013, including one hospitalised with liver damage; testing of the implicated B-50 supplements found methasterone, dimethazine and methylstenbolone, and symptoms of severe virilization were reported in a child [3]. Wikipedia more broadly reports that a 2007 to 2016 analysis found 776 supplements with unlisted pharmaceutical ingredients, including muscle-building products contaminated with anabolic steroids [5].

A 2014 case report in the Journal of Investigative Medicine High Impact Case Reports described what the authors called the first case of cholestatic jaundice linked to Super DMZ Rx 2.0, a product containing methylstenbolone and dymethazine. The patient was a previously healthy 26-year-old man who took the product as directed for 30 days, and the authors noted that such supplements may hide potent androgens from consumers [2]. A 2024 review of 50 years of case reports on anabolic-androgenic steroid abuse found methylstenbolone most strongly linked to hepatic complications [4]. Wikipedia categorises mebolazine among hepatotoxins [1].
No studies found testing mebolazine as a treatment or performance aid in people. Published human data are limited to case reports of harm from supplements that contained it [2][3].

timeline.event: Begins to appear as an undeclared ingredient in dietary supplements [1].
Reports of liver and other symptoms in New York residents using B-50 supplements containing dimethazine and other steroids [3].
Case report of cholestatic jaundice with a supplement containing dymethazine and methylstenbolone [2].
